real_conflicts: Replacing the solid house silhouettes with 'dithering' or 'pixel-sorting' effects (Visual Concept proposal) would destroy the necessary visual weight required to frame the composition. The current heavy black shapes act as the 'walls' of the corridor; if they dissolve into the background, the central perspective of the road loses its structural anchor, and the image becomes a flat, indistinct wash of color rather than a defined space.

Reducing the letter-spacing of the title to 'standard levels' (Typography proposal) would collapse the visual rhythm of the upper third. The wide tracking is essential to create a horizontal band of negative space that balances the vertical pull of the road. Standard tracking would make the title feel like a generic label rather than an atmospheric element that mimics the fading distance of the town.
accepted: Breaking the rigid symmetry of the layout by shifting the tagline 'Some places disappear twice' off the central axis. Currently, the text acts as a visual roadblock on the vanishing point; moving it allows the eye to travel uninterrupted down the road toward the light.

Introducing a subtle noise filter (Color/Atmosphere proposal) to break up the digital smoothness of the gradient. This adds a tactile quality that supports the theme of 'memory' without disrupting the spatial geometry.
concession: I concede that the current placement of the tagline is a compositional error. While I defend the symmetry of the houses, I agree that the text must not sit directly on the vanishing point. I will allow the tagline to be moved to the right or left margin to clear the central path.
compromise: We will maintain the heavy, solid silhouettes of the houses to preserve the 'corridor' effect, but we will break the symmetry of the text. The title remains wide and centered to cap the sky, but the tagline will be shifted to the right side, floating in the negative space near the horizon. This creates an asymmetrical balance that feels more cinematic and less like a template, while keeping the central road clear for the viewer's eye.
nonnegotiable: The central perspective of the road leading to the vanishing point must remain the dominant visual vector. No text or graphic element may obstruct the path from the bottom center to the light source.
